correctness.rationale: The unique reduced pole has order 7, prime to 3, which ensures a connected degree-three Artin–Schreier cover, totally ramified only at infinity. Its different exponent is 2(7+1)=16; Riemann–Hurwitz gives genus 6 and the one-branch-point Deuring–Shafarevich formula gives 3-rank zero. At the point over infinity, the orders of x and y are −3 and −7 and div(dx)=10P. Thus dx, x dx, x²dx, x³dx, y dx and xy dx are regular and have distinct orders; there are six. The separable coordinate x gives the Cartier rule retaining powers of x congruent to 2 modulo 3. Using y=y³−f, the only nonzero images are those of x²dx, y dx and xy dx: respectively dx, −(a^(1/3)x+c^(1/3))dx and −(x²+b^(1/3)x+d^(1/3))dx (the second image can vanish for special coefficients). These give first rank 3 iff a≠0, otherwise 2, second image exactly the line of dx and third image zero. The a-number is the kernel dimension; the reduced jumping locus in the marked coefficient chart is exactly the reduced irreducible hyperplane V(a), without a claim about a scheme structure in the unmarked stack.
